write_up: You’ve moved from Program Coordinator to Program Manager at Harbor Pathways, working with students, employers and funders. A recruiter can follow that path and see your management responsibilities. I’d move this forward for a youth workforce program role, with questions about how many students and employers the program reaches.

The summer jobs line is your best model: it names the program, the students and where they’re placed. Your supervision line also gives a recruiter a concrete view of your team. The rest of the recent role names useful work, but leaves the program’s reach and what the team handles less clear.

Let’s start with the summer jobs line, then add what your coordinators and seasonal staff do. From there, give the grant reports and employer partnerships a little more substance using details you can confirm.

cards.line: - Supervise 4 program coordinators and 20 seasonal staff
cards.cannot_tell: The team numbers are useful. What the coordinators and seasonal staff handle would show a recruiter more about the work you manage.

cards.line: - Write grant reports for city and foundation funders
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter knows who receives the reports, but not what you report on. The program information you pull together would make this work more concrete.

cards.line: - Recruit and onboard employer partners
cards.cannot_tell: Recruiting and onboarding are clear responsibilities, but the number of partners and what onboarding involves are missing.

cards.question: How many employer partners do you recruit and onboard, and what does onboarding involve?

cards.cannot_tell: The annual fair is a useful event to name. A recruiter can’t tell who attended or how many people it reached.
